The frontline employee safety plan update launched in June 2024 to improve workplace safety and foster a culture of safety within Saskatoon Transit.
All initiatives identified in the plan have been addressed and implemented except for the role load of the expected respectful and harassment free workplace policy, which is in progress.
We have received the opportunity to be improving safety for employees and riders by reducing the risk of negative reactions.
The goals are to maintain order on the bus, reduce negative interactions, and provide employees with the skills and tools they need to de-escalate situations.
The initiatives within the plan focused on the key areas of prevention and security, processes and procedures, training and education, responding to serious incidents in the culture of safety.
It has launched include an increase in uniform presence on buses and at terminals with patrols by transit supervisors and commissioners, the launch of fire community support team.
The creation of the rider band process enhanced customer service and de-escalation training for frontline employees, in health mental health supports two to three times each month.
Assessment Transit employees participate in a survey in February 2025 to measure awareness of and the satisfaction with the initiatives in the transit frontline employee safety plan.
Employees are aware of the plan and most felt that more time and additional efforts on these initiatives will help improve safety.
Assessment Transit also surveyed riders about safety on transit, with pushed notifications through the transit apps rate my ride, approximately 1,600 individuals responded each week.
And the results of the survey from November 25 to December 1 show that 97% of riders feel either very safe or fine.

The implementation of the Saskatoon Transit frontline employee safety plan in June 2024 and fire community support program in July 2024 has shown some early successes in meeting the goals of improving safety at Saskatoon Transit, whoever more work needs to be done to achieve the goal of all riders and employees feeling very safe on Saskatoon Transit.
Some of the next steps towards this goal include continuing to follow up on incidents and improve where possible based on employee feedback and the investigation process.

Prioritizing the list of improvements identified in the employee survey and work with Malcolm and the transit union, the Saskatoon Transit Occupational Health and Safety Committee and employees to improve safety.
We're going to continue to collaborate with Saskatoon Fire and the transit and the fire unions on implementing and refining the fire community support program for Saskatoon Transit.
We're going to continue to meet the with the city of Saskatoon interagency support team to discuss and mitigate current safety and security issues affecting Saskatoon Transit.

Extend the city's customer context standard respected public awareness campaign with Saskatoon Transit employee images on stickers and posters at Saskatoon Transit facilities and buses and digitally on the city's website and social media channels.

A coverage focus network prioritizes the availability of service where everyone has access regardless of where they live or their specific travel needs.
Coverage focus networks tend to prioritize walk distance and individual travel needs over convenience for the majority.
Ridership focus networks prioritize a frequent indirect service to generate the highest ridership where service offerings may not be equal to all areas.
The focus of a ridership driven network is on service quality and the needs of groups of riders. Next slide.
